agenda.say:
• Welcome; today starts John Doe's case from the beginning
• Part 1, all the lessons: the case, your role, facts vs. legal advice, reading the file, Case Plan, client directions, the car, client communications
• Part 2, the daily loop: meet John Doe on his Case Profile and do his Intake, our Skill Building, then write the Action Plan
• Six short side exercises after it are optional
• Knowledge Check: 70% opens Day 2

lab.say:
• Optional side exercises: each one an assumption and one entry to log in the CMS
• The backup folders, the Recorded Statement instruction, the PD file, the outreach log, the task set, the warning letter
• About 30 minutes, about five minutes each; then the Ready check

wrap.say:
• Robert Smith's insurer has already called John Doe, and he needs a car for work
• Discuss what to tell him today, in what order
• Cover: the do's and don'ts in plain words and the rental path
• Log every step the same day; route anything legal to Atty. Thorne
• What John says this week stays in the adjuster's notes for the life of the case
wrap.ask: What would you tell John Doe first, and why first?

lifemap.say:
• The whole of John Doe's file on one slide, in the order we work it this week
• Across the top: the six stages you carry on every file
• Day 1 it's raw: the loss, the SOL docketed, the matter opened in the CMS
• Then claims and care, the demand, liens and ADR, and litigation to the close
• Each day picks the file up where the last one left it
lifemap.ask: Which one date on this track would you protect first, and why?

coverage.say:
• Three layers pay in order: BI $10,000, Host UM $20,000, Relative UM $10,000
• $40,000 is the cap, so the care and records must prove value through all three
• Before any BI release: the UM consent to settle and the subrogation waiver
• The Health Plan pays care now and recovers from the settlement, so plan the reduction early
• The gap before treatment is the weak point: name it on Day 1, with its reason documented
coverage.ask: If the BI adjuster offered the full $10,000 tomorrow, what must be on the file before anyone says yes?

plan.say:
• Step 4 of the loop, guided: the Action Plan template, section by section, on the shared screen
• Every fact from the Intake with the document it comes from; every action item with an owner, a date and a tool
• Anything only Atty. Thorne decides is routed to him, with the date

agenda.say:
• Welcome back; today covers John Doe's claim set-up and treatment
• Claim set-up lessons: coverage tracking, affidavits, liability, decision-first notes, LORs; then the treatment plan and Case Plan
• Treatment lessons: payers, LOPs, EOBs, PIP strategy, the EMC rule, costs, health subrogation, A-C-T monitoring
• Part 2, the daily loop: the Case Profile, then one Skill Building, the LORs to all three carriers, then update the Action Plan
• Nine short side exercises after it are optional
• Knowledge Check: 70% opens Day 3

lab.say:
• Optional side exercises: each one an assumption and one entry to log in the CMS
• The policy stack, the matrix audit, the gap flag, the Case Plan, the LOPs, the redirected referral, the lien, the near-drop, the backup
• About 30 minutes: time for about six of them, so each trainee chooses six; then the Ready check

wrap.say:
• Scenario 04/08/2026: Keystone confirmed its limit in writing 03/20; Riverton Spine & Rehab reports two missed visits
• Dana Whitfield has asked John Doe for a Recorded Statement
• Discuss first, second and third steps and what each protects
• Cover: stop the recorded call through the firm that day; reach John on every approved channel and log it
• Missed visits go to Atty. Thorne with facts and a plan; ask why before assuming
wrap.ask: Which of those three moves comes first, and what does it protect?

profile.say:
• Step 2 of the loop: a minute on John Doe's Case Profile, The Case So Far
• Since yesterday: the matter is open and three claims were reported by phone, nothing in writing yet
• Ask what has to be confirmed in writing first, then straight into the Skill Building

plan.say:
• Step 4: update the Action Plan on your own, about ten minutes
• Every claim now open, with its carrier and claim number; the next action items with owners and dates

agenda.say:
• Welcome back; from Day 2: when John's ride ended, ask the clinic about transportation help, log it, tell Atty. Thorne
• Lessons: the Gap Explanation Record, pre-demand case auditing, the demand, settlement negotiations, the UM consent and waiver, the settlement release
• Part 2, the daily loop: the Case Profile, then one Skill Building, serving the BI demand, then update the Action Plan
• Thirteen short side exercises after it are optional
• Knowledge Check: 70% opens Day 4

lab.say:
• Optional side exercises: each one an assumption and one entry to log in the CMS
• The gap call and record, wages and Specials, the strategy decisions, the backup audit, the UM demands, the offer, the release, both Net Sheets
• About 30 minutes: time for about six of them, so each trainee chooses six; then the Ready check

wrap.say:
• 07/20/2026: Specials audited; Atty. Thorne approved a policy-limits demand to Keystone
• Discuss what must be true before the Time-Limited Demand goes out
• Cover: every record and bill included, numbers matching the audit, a clear reasonable deadline, proof of receipt, Atty. Thorne's sign-off
• One missing page lets Keystone argue it never had a fair chance to settle
• Next: the $40,000 gross meets the bills, and how it gets split
wrap.ask: What must be true before the Time-Limited Demand goes out to Keystone?

profile.say:
• Step 2 of the loop: John Doe's Case Profile, The Case So Far
• Treatment is complete: MMI 06/12/2026, Specials $16,401.40, the gap still to be explained from his documents
• Then straight into the Skill Building: the BI demand

plan.say:
• Step 4: update the Action Plan: where the demand stands and the next deadline
• A lighter touch today: the trainees write it, you spot-check two plans

agenda.say:
• Welcome back; today covers the money side of Track A, the settled file, then Track B, where it doesn't settle
• Lessons: liens and provider balances, reductions, the Net Sheet, the release audit, disbursement and closing, court rules, mediation and arbitration, the binders
• Part 2, the daily loop: the Case Profile, then one Skill Building, the Mediation Binder, then update the Action Plan
• Twelve short side exercises after it are optional
• Knowledge Check: 70% opens Day 5

lab.say:
• Optional side exercises: each one an assumption and one entry to log in the CMS
• The two lien reductions, the final Net Sheet, the prior-attorney lien, the disbursement, the backup, the impasse, the calendars, the ADR matrix, the Arbitration Binder
• About 30 minutes: time for about six of them, so each trainee chooses six; then the Ready check

wrap.say:
• John Doe's net from the $40,000 is $20,359.92
• Scenario: Keystone's draft release arrives 08/14/2026, releasing "all other persons, firms, corporations and insurers"
• Harbor Point hasn't answered the consent request; Atty. Thorne is out until Monday
• Flag that language, since it could release the UM insurers; chase Harbor Point's consent in writing; log everything
• Nothing gets signed until Atty. Thorne reviews it
wrap.ask: What must not happen before Atty. Thorne is back, and why?

profile.say:
• Step 2 of the loop: John Doe's Case Profile, The Case So Far
• Track A settled at $40,000 gross; liens still to resolve; Track B heads to mediation and arbitration
• Then straight into the Skill Building: the Mediation Binder

plan.say:
• Step 4: update the Action Plan: the binder's exchange date and what Atty. Thorne still decides
• The trainees work alone; spot-check that every item has an owner and a date

agenda.say:
• Welcome back to the last day: Litigation and Dropped Cases on John Doe's file
• Lessons, about 30 minutes: the litigation fork and filing, bottlenecks, litigation tracking, trial prep, depositions, the award, Dropped Cases
• Part 2, the daily loop: the Case Profile, then the Full Application Practice, about three hours on the assigned companion case
• Then close out the Action Plan; John's 15 side exercises are optional
• Knowledge Check: 70% finishes the Case Flow

lab.say:
• Practice Lab: 15 Skill Activities on John Doe's file in the CMS, optional extra practice today
• Litigation fork and litigation status, e-filing the Complaint and calendaring service, CMS countermeasures, a bottleneck
• Pleadings and discovery logs, trial-prep checklist audit, Keystone's final Property Damage position, deposition prep, mock cross-examination
• Liability counter-package, skip-tracing, Litigation Net Sheet, final backup audit, Denise Harlow's Dropped Case
• Calendar everything each task starts; in litigation a missed date can end the claim

wrap.say:
• 01/05/2027: opposing counsel's paralegal says discovery responses are late; John Doe changed his number; deposition set 02/18/2027
• Confirm the real discovery deadline on the calendar; tell Atty. Thorne today
• Start outreach on every approved channel and log it; if John stays silent, begin the skip-trace steps
• Protect the deposition date; more time, or what to tell the other side, is Atty. Thorne's call
• Late discovery can cost the client evidence and money
wrap.ask: What do you do today, in what order, and what is Atty. Thorne's call, not yours?

build.say:
• Full Application Practice: the rest of the day, about three hours, building the assigned companion case, worked like John Doe's file
• Step 1, read the file; step 2, open it in the CMS, Conflict Check first on every party's full legal name
• Step 3, the folder by the SOP: [Your Full Name] - [Case Name], nine subfolders, connected, intake documents uploaded
• Step 4, the claims: every carrier in the stack, Letters of Representation, verification status, coverage matrix
• Time is called at each step; each case has its own problem to find
build.ask: What is the first fact on your case to confirm, and where?

extra.say:
• Optional extra practice: John Doe's 15 Day 5 Skill Activities, untimed
• Today's practical was the companion case
• Worth coming back to soon: the deposition prep and the Dropped Case close-out
• Most rooms skip these: the skip button goes to the Ready check, then the Knowledge Check

build2.say:
• Second half: steps 5 to 7
• Step 5, plan the care: treatment map, 14-day rule and any gap, who pays first, whether an LOP is needed
• LOP, Letter of Protection: the firm's written promise to pay a provider from the settlement
• Step 6, the Case Notes entry for Atty. Thorne: decision first, then the deadline it hangs on
• Step 7, check the work: every document in the CMS and case folder, CMS Case ID logged
build2.ask: What decision does the note to Atty. Thorne lead with?

profile.say:
• Step 2 of the loop: John Doe's Case Profile, The Case So Far
• Track B: the demand lapsed, suit filed 09/24/2026, discovery and the deposition ahead
• Then straight into the Full Application Practice

plan.say:
• Step 4: close out the Action Plan: the litigation handoff, what is still open, the sign-off
• A few minutes, on their own
